system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**CONFIDENTIAL – BUYER LEGAL ADVICE**  
**Project Kestrel – Seller SPA Mark-Up & Disclosure Letter Review**  
Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Principal: Amelia Frost)  
Date: 23 September 2026  

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Seller’s updated SPA and Disclosure Letter **depart materially from the Playbook on every core protection**. The draft attempts to collapse fundamental/title warranties into a diluted general regime, impose a sub‑Playbook cap without authority, widen thresholds five‑fold, cut the claims period to an unapproved fallback, extend limitations to fraud/wilful misconduct, replace specific disclosure with whole‑data‑room deemed disclosure, impose a blanket buyer‑knowledge bar, and leave Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, and title evidence unresolved on terms the Playbook expressly rejects. **No Playbook position has been met.** A full re‑mark is required; we cannot sign on this basis.

---

### CLAUSE‑BY‑CLAUSE DEPARTURES & REASONING

| # | Playbook Position | Seller Draft | Departure & Risk | Push‑Back Required |
|---|-------------------|--------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **1** | **General cap: 25% / AUD 6M** (starting). 20% / AUD 4.8M **only with Amelia Frost written authority** (none given). | **20% / AUD 4.8M** (Cl. 12.1). | Seller proposes our **fallback cap as opening bid** without the required principal sign‑off. This reduces headroom by AUD 1.2M. | Reject. Restate 25% / AUD 6M. Flag that 20% is not authorised. |
| **2** | **De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k (tipping – first dollar once exceeded).** | **De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (excess‑only / deductible).** (Cl. 12.2). | Thresholds **5× wider**; basket type changed from tipping to deductible – Seller bears **zero** liability until aggregate claims exceed AUD 250k, then only the excess. | Revert to AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket. |
| **3** | **General claims: 24 months.** 18 months fallback **needs Amelia Frost written approval** (none). **Fundamental/Title: separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** | **18 months for all claims** (Cl. 12.3/13). **Limitations apply to ALL claims unless expressly stated otherwise.** **Fundamental/Title collapsed into general regime** (same caps, same time limits). | Seller imposes **unapproved fallback period** and **eliminates the separate fundamental/title regime** entirely – title/capacity claims would be subject to 20% cap, 18‑month limit, basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar. | **Non‑negotiable:** Separate fundamental/title regime at 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier. General period 24 months. |
| **4** | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non‑reliance. No waiver permitted.** | **Limitations, exclusive‑remedy, non‑reliance apply to “all Claims of any nature”** (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5). | **Direct contradiction** – Seller’s drafting would bar fraud/wilful misconduct claims via caps, baskets, time bars, and non‑reliance clauses. | Insert express carve‑out for fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from **every** limitation provision. |
| **5** | **Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole‑data‑room, public‑register, prudent‑search deemed disclosure.** | **General disclosure of entire data room (DD‑002 to DD‑012) + public registers + statutory registers** (Disclosure Letter §1.1, 1.2). | **Whole‑data‑room disclosure** is exactly what the Playbook prohibits – it shifts review burden to Buyer and creates “deemed knowledge” arguments. | Delete general disclosure. Require **specific, document‑by‑document fair disclosure** with page‑level references. |
| **6** | **Delete blanket buyer‑knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier: named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity.** | **“Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records”** (Cl. 8.3). | **Blanket buyer‑knowledge bar** covering data‑room and public records – **exactly the clause the Playbook forbids**. Would extinguish claims for matters Buyer “could have found”. | Strike Cl. 8.3 entirely. If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to **named Seller individuals + reasonable enquiry**, and **exclude title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnities**. |
| **7** | **Bluefen: effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.** | **Reasonable endeavours; consent “treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent”** (Cl. 3/6.3). **Disclosure confirms NO final written consent, NO evidence conditions satisfied** (DL §2). | Seller offers **only reasonable endeavours** and **consent‑on‑delivery** (post‑signing, pre‑Completion at best). No pre‑Completion certainty; conditions in Cl. 11.3 unaddressed. | **Condition Precedent:** Bluefen written consent **and** evidence all Cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied **before Completion**. No “reasonable endeavours” fallback for a material customer consent. |
| **8** | **Riverlark: current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post‑Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.** | **“Release to be provided following Completion”** (Cl. 2/7). **Disclosure: facility NOT repaid, NO final discharge** (DL §3). | **Post‑Completion release only**, no irrevocable undertaking, no Amelia Frost approval mechanism. Buyer funds would discharge Seller’s debt **after** Completion with no enforceable commitment. | **Completion‑funds payout** directly to Riverlark with simultaneous security discharge. If Seller insists on post‑Completion, require **irrevocable undertaking + Frost written approval** (not given). |
| **9
=== END ADVICE ===
